increment_paragraph: **LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY** (Fluent Bit queue, P1.3 retry and backlog routes; gateway rule 43, rules 10f(3) and 34 amended, contract specification §C04.8 amended, qcore-schemas 25.0.0 `ContainerEffect::ElementsReleased`, Lean `QCore.ElementReleaseSummary`; [report](../../reports/list-entry-release-identity/README.md)). The census of release actuals at base `74105dd0e` found the dominant generic refusal to be a list element of a formal-rooted container released by a declared destroyer (system 50 of 160 destroyer leaves, slice 11): rule 10f(2) gives such an element an identity only at an unlink and no destroyer stated one. Ten Fluent Bit destroyers whose bodies call `mk_list_del(&P->_head)` before `flb_free(P)` at the three trees now declare `resource_unpublished(P)` (re-pinned), and the loader admits that clause beside rule 30's member-path states, which seven of them carry. Rule 43 lets an element destroyer take an object the path already holds (live, unpublished, unlinked on no path), so formal hand-offs keep their release, and lets a body whose element custody is rooted at its formals publish its summary with `ElementsReleased` there; a caller forgets every object it published and carries the clause on. Measured on the card's own preparations: system custody 103/4/341 → 107/4/337 (`flb_engine_destroy_tasks`, `flb_storage_input_destroy`, both configurations), slice 58/1/341/4 Pending → 59/1/340/4 (`flb_tail_file_remove_all`), exactly the predicted moves (arbiter declaration check: match), no Safe row moved, null tallies unchanged; corpus 1,079/6/3,619 → 1,081/6/3,617, two unpredicted Monkey rows (`mk_sched_threads_purge`, `mk_sched_threads_destroy_all`) made Safe by the released-element summary of their in-unit drain `sched_thread_cleanup`, read and attributed; per configuration 27 system and 9 slice unresolved-identity leaves resolved and 28/14 unlink refusals added beside already-refused releases. On the system and slice routes the summary reaches no caller (every caller is in another unit); OR-6 is unchanged.
status_paragraph: LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY (gateway rule 43, measured base `74105dd0e` against tip `f4057708f` on the card's own preparations of the three live routes): a released list element of a formal-rooted container now has an identity at a declared element destroyer (ten Fluent Bit destroyers state `resource_unpublished`), and a body whose element custody is rooted at its formals publishes an `ElementsReleased` summary. System custody 103/4/341 → 107/4/337, slice 58/1/341/4 Pending → 59/1/340/4, corpus 1,079/6/3,619 → 1,081/6/3,617 (two Monkey scheduler drains' callers); no Safe row moved and no Unsafe was added. Derived summaries stay in their unit, so on the Fluent Bit routes no caller consumes the clause; OR-6 is not stated.

ledger.why: DISCHARGED by LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY (gateway rule 43): a body whose every element custody (foreign unlink or applied clause) is rooted at its formals publishes its derived summary with ContainerEffect::ElementsReleased at exactly those formals (W4 gate exact, attached by infer_cfg_summary; any static, local or callee root still withholds it); a caller applying the clause drops every published site (each withdrawn with an unresolved effect, so a later unlink, release or use refuses) and carries the clause on for its own formal. Lean QCore.ElementReleaseSummary (forgetting_covers_every_release, the_gate_is_exact, the_borrowed_reading_would_trust_a_released_object); fixtures crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/element_release_summary.rs with a rule-43-off child. Measured: on the corpus two Monkey callers of the in-unit drain sched_thread_cleanup move Unknown -> Safe on it; on the system and slice routes every caller is in another unit (LERI-CROSS-UNIT-ELEMENTS-RELEASED); the cited flb_task_queue_destroy cost is moot (it is now a declared destroyer).

ledger.text: ADVANCED by LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY (gateway rule 43, measured at 74105dd0e on the card's preparations): the list-entry shape is decided. Ten destroyers declare resource_unpublished (bodies read at the three trees, re-pinned), the loader admits it beside member-path states, and rule 43 lets a destroyer take a held object; system 27 and slice 9 unresolved-identity leaves per configuration resolved, flb_engine_destroy_tasks and flb_storage_input_destroy (system, both configurations) and flb_tail_file_remove_all (slice) Unknown -> Safe, every moved row read. Still open: the actuals that are not admitted elements, held or published objects (system 42 'other' and 10 'formal' leaves, slice 44 and 16; the slice's flb_tail_config_create/in_tail_init `ctx` local; poisoned formals), which now also report `unlink by DESTROYER of X, which this function has not published` beside their release (28 system, 14 slice per configuration), and the member-read actuals (system 16).

AMENDED by LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY (gateway rule 43): the summary half now exists (a body with formal-rooted element custody publishes ElementsReleased), but flb_output_task_queue_flush_one and flb_output_task_singleplex_flush_next are a mutually recursive pair: neither row is Safe on its own, so neither publishes first, and the recursive-component routes do not attach the clause. Re-measured at 74105dd0e: both rows unchanged (no leaf moved). OR-6 stays not stated; the blocker is now the recursive component's summary, not the vocabulary.

AMENDED by LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY (gateway rule 43): a container-ownership summary for list elements exists for derived bodies (ElementsReleased at a formal whose list a body drains through an element destroyer or a foreign unlink); of the six undeclared teardown functions, flb_engine_destroy_tasks is now Safe with that clause in its unit; flb_task_retry_clean, flb_sched_request_invalidate, flb_output_exit, flb_input_exit_all and flb_tail_file_remove_all (Safe on the slice) are each blocked by other leaves or reached only from other units. No declared form of the clause exists (LERI-ELEMENTS-RELEASED-DECLARED-FORM); P-B08-SHALLOW is unchanged for members.

Checked by LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY: its element identities are plain names bound to sites, its clause only withdraws sites and it adds no Stored or Removed mode, so it puts no projection-bound place on an admitted chain; TrackedBasesAreBound is not exercised by it.

ledger.title: An ElementsReleased summary reaches no caller in another unit, and every Fluent Bit caller is in one
ledger.text: Card LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY measured (74105dd0e, its own preparations; on the corpus the clause does reach in-unit Monkey callers, mk_sched_threads_purge and mk_sched_threads_destroy_all becoming Safe): the bodies that now validate with ElementsReleased (flb_engine_destroy_tasks, flb_storage_input_destroy, flb_tail_file_remove_all) are called only from other units (flb_input_instance_destroy, in_tail_exit, flb_tail_config_destroy), which still read `call to uncontracted function`; flb_output_exit, flb_sched_timer_cleanup, flb_task_retry_clean and flb_sched_destroy are likewise reached from other units or still Unknown. DISCHARGE: carry derived summaries (with their container effects, so a consumer that cannot apply ElementsReleased refuses) across units through the link-standing route, then re-measure the system and slice callers with every moved row read.

ledger.title: ElementsReleased has no declared form, and a declaration that omits it is compared on custody only
ledger.text: Card LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY states ElementsReleased only in derived summaries (rendered resource_elements_released(#i) in the clause standing). A declared contract for a body that drains a formal's list (flb_task_queue_destroy) is compared with the derived summary on custody projections, so the declaration's silence about elements is a declared assumption, not a conflict. DISCHARGE: a declared `resource_elements_released(p)` clause (grammar, loader, body check against the derived clause) and a decision whether a declaration without it, for a body that needs it, is a conflict; then declare the six list-entry teardown functions where no unit defines them.

ledger.title: Rule 43's P-LERI-HELD-LINKS and P-LERI-LINK-MEMBER are stated, not proved
ledger.text: Rule 43 admits an element destroyer's unlink of an object the path holds and never unlinked under P-LERI-HELD-LINKS (its links are ones an unlink may remove: linked, or initialised; a freshly allocated object with NULL links would fault in mk_list_del, a memory-safety obligation outside the custody projection), and reads resource_unpublished, which names no link member, as removing the object from the list a caller iterates (P-LERI-LINK-MEMBER; flb_tail_file_remove unlinks _rotate_head only while file->rotated > 0). P-LERI-CALLER-PUBLISHED (the only tracked objects a container the actual reaches may hold are the caller's published ones) is likewise stated. DISCHARGE: a link-state obligation on the destroyer's entry (initialised or linked) decided from the body's own initialisation, and a link-member field in resource_unpublished checked against the caller's container_of member, each with Lean parity; or a measured statement of where each premise is load-bearing.

ledger.title: Seven re-pinned destroyers record the tail-pause tree as upstream 90978ac6, not the synthetic export 34155955
ledger.text: Card LIST-ENTRY-RELEASE-IDENTITY re-pinned the ten destroyers whose text it changed; the slice tree available to it was a quirin-audit prepare of upstream 90978ac6 (the export's tree), so the identities read there are recorded at git 90978ac6 where the earlier pins named the synthetic 34155955. pin --check exits 1 at each tree with the pre-existing not-in-force set only; whether the published slice preparation (34155955) reads these declarations in force through another revision was not measured. DISCHARGE: run pin --check (and the slice route) on the published preparation at the landing and re-pin there if any of the seven is not in force.
